subject: Request: Subprocessor list + dataflow proof for CachePulse caching microservice
body:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ramos <emily@fastcache.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Subprocessor list + dataflow proof for CachePulse caching microservice

Hi Emily —

Quick note from the Redwood procurement/compliance side. We’re validating the last-mile caching component you mentioned in the SOW (CachePulse). Before we can sign off on the onboarding runbook we need: 

- A current subprocessor roster used by CachePulse (names, country, processing role).
- A simple dataflow diagram (image or PDF) showing where customer request/response payloads traverse and which subprocessors may touch token-level or request metadata.
- Confirmation of whether CachePulse or any of its subprocessors perform any of the following: temporary persistence of prompt/response payloads, telemetry event export to third parties, or encrypted key material storage outside your KMS.

We’d like redacted artifacts where necessary — a CSV export and the dataflow image is fine. Can you send this by Monday (20 Jul)? If you have a SOC 2 report or equivalent, a redacted copy delivered via secure link would speed review.

Thanks — trying to keep the procurement window tight.

Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---

From: Emily Ramos <emily@fastcache.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Subprocessor list + dataflow proof for CachePulse caching microservice

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear list. See attached: fastcache_subprocessor_list_v1.csv and cachepulse_dataflow_v1.png. The CSV lists our downstream vendors and the processing role for each. Short summary: none of our subprocessors persist customer prompt/response payloads beyond the caching TTL (default 2 hours) except where customers opt-in to analytics—those exports are handled by TelemetryHub (listed in CSV).

We do keep short-lived telemetry for performance — anonymized metrics and sampling indicators. No key material is stored outside our KMS; we use AWS KMS and have a BYOK option.

I can share a redacted SOC 2 Type II via secure link if you’d like — we’ll remove customer-identifying artifacts. Also attaching a one-page diagram.

Attachments: fastcache_subprocessor_list_v1.csv (text/csv), cachepulse_dataflow_v1.png (image/png)

Best,
Emily Ramos
Head of Customer Security
FastCache, Inc.

On Mon, Jul 20, 2026 at 08:30 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:

> Emily —
>
> Thanks for the files. Two follow-ups from the security engineering side: 
> 1) We need confirmation that TelemetryHub’s retention and export controls meet our minimum: 90-day aggregated metrics, no raw prompt/response export to third parties unless explicitly autorized per-customer. Please specify export destinations (S3 buckets, partner endpoints) and whether any are cross-border.
> 2) Please provide the address of the KMS/HSM tenant for the CachePulse runtime; we need to confirm whether a subprocessor (or your ops team) can access plaintext keys/derivatives. If fastcache uses a managed HSM, include the vendor and region.
>
> If you can upload the SOC 2 redacted PDF to the drive link Kimberly included we’ll get the initial pass.
>
> Thanks,
> Ben
> Security & Reliability Engineering
> Redwood Inference

-----Original message-----
From: Emily Ramos <emily@fastcache.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 13:15:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Subprocessor list + dataflow proof for CachePulse caching microservice

Ben / Kimberly —

Appreciate the detailed asks. Quick answers inline: 

1) TelemetryHub retention/export: TelemetryHub retains sampled telemetry for 90 days by default. Exports to partner endpoints are opt-in and customer-scoped; current outbound destinations are: 
   - s3://fastcache-telemetry-prod-us (AWS us-east-1) 
   - https://ingest.partner-analytics.com/ingest (TLS, partner contract in place)
   Both are explicitly logged and require an export flag per-customer. No raw prompt/response payloads are exported unless a customer enables the analytics add-on.

2) KMS/HSM: CachePulse keys are managed in an AWS KMS customer master key (alias: alias/fastcache/cachepulse) in us-east-1. We do not store plaintext keys; only the runtime has access via role-based short-lived credentials. We do have an optional HSM-backed key for customers who require it (through CloudHSM, vendor: cryptaHSM, region: us-east-1).

SOC 2: I’ve uploaded a redacted SOC 2 Type II (fastcache_soc2_redacted.pdf) to a secure DocShare link — here: https://docshare.fastcache.io/s/abcd-1234 (link expires in 14 days). Additionally, we’ve created a DocuSign envelope for the Redwood subprocessor addendum: https://docusign.com/DocuSignEnvelope/fastcache-subproc-addendum

Attachments: fastcache_soc2_redacted.pdf (application/pdf)

Let me know if you need the full non-redacted SOC 2 under an NDA; we can coordinate that with legal.

Best,
Emily

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 11:02:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Subprocessor list + dataflow proof for CachePulse caching microservice

Emily —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Two commercial items to align on: 

- Can FastCache accept the standard Redwood subprocessor addendum (we sent a markup last week)? If so, sign + return to the DocuSign link and we’ll route to procurement.
- We’ll need a proposed cutover/onboarding schedule that includes: evidence handoff, SOC2 review window, canary deployment window (we usually do a 72-hour canary), and rollback criteria.

Marissa, assigning to you to track procurement items once we have confirmation.

Thanks,
Jordan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Subprocessor list + dataflow proof for CachePulse caching microservice

Emily —

This looks good; thank you for the artifacts. Two quick next steps from Redwood Privacy/Compliance: 

1) Please sign the subprocessor addendum via DocuSign by EOD Friday (23 Jul) so we can attach it to the DPA.
2) Upload the redacted SOC 2 PDF to the shared drive link (https://drive.redwood.com/shared/CachePulse-evidence) so our team can annotate sections for the security review. If you need an NDA for the non-redacted report, we’ll loop legal — but the redacted one should suffice for initial intake.

We’ll target an internal sign-off by 30 Jul conditional on the addendum and the SOC 2 review. If anything blocking pops up Ben will reach out with a narrow list of evidence requests.

Appreciate the speed on this — Kimberly
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
